source_title: EHRGym: Epic-like EHR environment for training and evaluating computer-use agents
locator: README sections Clinical focus, What you get, Quickstart, and GRPO Training with TRL; repository license metadata
source_setting: Public GitHub software repository; synthetic EHR UI and browser-controlled OpenEnv environment, stated to be unaffiliated with Epic.
source_period: Repository snapshot observed 2026-10-10; repository is an actively changing public project.
source_evidence_basis: GitHub README describes a Next.js EHR, FastAPI/OpenEnv server with Playwright, synthetic patient pipeline, provider-oriented tasks, and Apache-2.0 license; it links to source directories and setup instructions.
limitations: README and license metadata establish what the repository documents and its stated open-source license, not that a clean install/build or hosted Space was independently run or that workflows match Epic or RWJBarnabas configuration. Do not equate this agent-computer-use environment with a validated human clinical training product or actual Epic software. Synthetic-only instruction is project guidance, not independent privacy/security certification.
inferred_scenario_use: Candidate sandbox for prototyping and scoring navigation, chart review, documentation, and order-workflow tasks with synthetic cases. Before use, inspect current source, dependency/license notices, scenario rubrics, hosted service controls, and reproducibility; require clinician review of any clinical rubric.

source_title: EHRGym: Epic-like EHR environment for training and evaluating computer-use agents
locator: README, sections 25 Clinical Tasks, Logging and Evaluation, and Safety
source_n: README claims 25 tasks: 8 basic, 9 medium, 8 hard.
quantity: Documented tasks and proposed evaluation metrics
source_evidence_basis: README lists the task counts and case types and proposes deterministic fixed-seed test suites and task/reward metrics.
limitations: These are repository README claims and proposed measurement dimensions, not independently reproduced benchmark results, validated clinical competency scores, or evidence of reduced patient harm. Task/rubric validity and annotation reliability are not established by the counts.
inferred_scenario_use: Use task counts only as a candidate scope estimate; define local competency outcomes and human-audited safety errors before comparing learner or model performance.

source_title: Epic on FHIR Developer Testing Guide: Epic Instances and Environments
locator: Developer Testing Guide, Epic Instances and Environments, especially FHIR Developer Sandbox paragraphs
source_setting: Epic FHIR Developer Sandbox, a shared testing environment; Epic distinguishes each customer's own training, test, reporting, support, and production environments.
source_n: One Epic-provided FHIR Sandbox; documentation says it refreshes weekly on Sunday about 8 p.m. Central and prior-week written data is erased.
source_evidence_basis: Epic documents separate customer instances and environments, identifies its single public FHIR Sandbox as a developer-testing resource, and describes weekly refresh and quarterly-version upgrade downtime.
limitations: The public FHIR Sandbox is for API development/testing, not a full customer-specific Epic Hyperspace training playground or faithful RWJBH workflow replica. Capabilities and configuration differ across customer instances; sandbox persistence is limited. Documentation describes APIs and testing, not human learner outcomes.
inferred_scenario_use: Use for integration/API proof-of-concept only. A local agent-training simulator could model workflows but should be clearly labeled separate from Epic and validated against authorized site-specific workflows before any training-transfer claim.

locator: For Developers clauses 5–6; For Everyone clauses 3–4
source_setting: Epic open.epic materials and testing sandbox terms for developers.

value.performance_scalability_security_testing: not intended and should not be used
value.direct_software_access: requires approval from Epic and an Epic Community Member

source_evidence_basis: Epic terms expressly state the sandbox simulates an EHR for testing, must contain only sample/synthetic data, may be wiped, is not for performance/scalability/security testing, and direct Epic software access requires both customer and Epic approval.
limitations: Terms do not describe RWJBH-specific access, build, or training permissions, nor establish equivalence between an independent simulator and Epic.
inferred_scenario_use: Maintain separate synthetic training data and avoid using the public sandbox as a throughput benchmark or as proof of readiness for a hospital deployment.

source_title: About the Department of Emergency Medicine: Clerkship Overview
locator: Clerkship Overview; clinical services and Rapid Decision Unit sections
source_setting: Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School Emergency Medicine clerkship and Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital (RWJUH), New Brunswick, NJ; affiliated rotation sites also include Somerset and Monmouth.
source_period: Current public program description accessed 2026-10-10; no training year or cohort dates given.
source_n: No learner cohort denominator reported. Page currently describes adult ED volume as over 80,000 visits annually; another page section says approximately 95,000, so neither should be treated as a reconciled current count.
value: Rapid Decision Unit for extended evaluation, treatment, monitoring, and disposition planning
source_evidence_basis: Official Rutgers RWJMS page lists clerkship length, supervision, simulation formats, rotation sites, and RDU workflow purpose.
limitations: This is a public description of emergency-medicine education and service pathways, not an EHR-specific curriculum, task-level RWJBH/Epic workflow specification, or measured efficacy study. Public page contains differing annual-volume statements in separate sections; neither figure is used as a calibrated denominator here.
inferred_scenario_use: Potential local context for case design around supervised ED care and observation/disposition, subject to clinician/faculty confirmation. Do not infer local staffing, Epic configuration, exact triage pathway, timing, or competency outcomes from this page.

source_title: Impact of Electronic Medical Record Training on Pediatric Residents’ Learning Outcomes: A Simulation-Based Study
locator: Abstract; Methods—Study design, Participants and Simulations; Results—Primary outcome; Table 1 and Figure 1
source_setting: Single-center prospective, parallel, non-blinded randomized controlled study at Riley Children’s Health, Indianapolis, using Cerner and simulated pediatric sepsis and respiratory-distress encounters.
source_period: August 2021–June 2022; follow-up simulations 3–6 months after baseline.
source_n: 32 first-year pediatric residents randomized 1:1 (16/group); 28 completed baseline and follow-up (14/group). All recruited residents participated in baseline simulations. Participants were from pediatrics, child neurology, neurodevelopmental, and child psychiatry; medicine-pediatrics residents excluded.
quantity: Change in EMR proficiency checklist score, sepsis scenario, baseline to follow-up; group means with 95% CI
source_evidence_basis: Randomized intervention received structured debriefing plus EMR-specific training; control received the same debriefing without EMR training. Authors report significantly greater improvement in the trained group for sepsis EMR checklist score. The secondary outcomes assessed simulated decision making/performance, not care delivered to actual patients.
limitations: Small single-site cohort; non-blinded; local Cerner-specific checklist; 4/32 randomized participants did not complete follow-up. Both groups had simulation/debriefing exposure; contrast estimates the additional EMR training intervention in this setting. Findings are learner assessment and simulated clinical performance only, not actual patient outcomes. Authors explicitly state actual-clinical-setting improvement remains to be demonstrated.
inferred_scenario_use: Supports a cautious hypothesis that structured EHR training may improve data-gathering proficiency in subsequent simulated cases. It does not validate EHRGym, establish transfer from agent task rewards to clinician competence, or show fewer errors/mortality/LOS in real patients. For local evaluation, predefine human learner outcomes and a later clinical-transfer study.
